title: Server Components
description: Use Minerva with React Server Components: which entries are client boundaries, what can run on the server and where to import the CSS.

entries.title: Entries and the "use client" banner
entries.text: @minerva/lib-core is published as several entries. The entries that contain components start with a "use client" directive; the theme helper entry does not, so it can run inside Server Components.
entries.main: All components, providers, hooks and utilities.
entries.monaco: The Monaco-based code editor (optional peers: @monaco-editor/react and monaco-editor).
entries.themeUtils: Server-safe theme helpers: THEME_INIT_SCRIPT, cookie parsing and serialization, palette names.
entries.utils: Server-safe utilities: cn, themes, light, dark, githubDark, palettes, resolveTheme, generateCSSVariables, applyThemeStyles, getSystemTheme, isBilingualTheme, matchesShortcut, normalizeShortcuts, computeFixedColumnLayout.

why.title: Why some entries are client boundaries
why.p1: Every Minerva component uses state, effects, context or portals, so it must run in the browser. Because the main entry is marked "use client", a Server Component that imports it does not get the component code: it gets client references, placeholders that the bundler resolves to the client bundle. The components are still rendered to HTML on the server during SSR and hydrated in the browser.
why.p2: A client reference is not a callable function on the server. That is fine for components, which are only rendered, but it means plain functions from a client entry cannot be executed in a Server Component. Functions needed on the server, such as parsing the theme cookie or building the init script, therefore live in a separate entry without the banner: @minerva/lib-core/theme-utils.

render.title: Rendering components from a Server Component
render.text: Import components from @minerva/lib-core directly in a Server Component, a layout or a page: no wrapper is needed, because the entry already is a client boundary.
render.props: Props passed from a Server Component to a client component must be serializable: strings, numbers, booleans, plain objects, arrays and JSX. Functions are not, so event handlers such as onClick, render props and callbacks need a small client component of your own:

functions.title: Calling functions on the server
functions.text: Call the helpers of @minerva/lib-core/theme-utils and @minerva/lib-core/utils freely on the server: in layouts, route handlers, middleware or edge functions. Do not call functions from the main entry in a Server Component (toast.success, Confirm, the hooks...), and do not read its data exports (themes, palettes...) there: they are client references. Import the plain functions and data from @minerva/lib-core/utils instead.
functions.imperative: Imperative APIs are also safe during SSR of client components: without a document they do nothing, and promise-based dialogs such as Confirm resolve to false on the server. Trigger them from event handlers or effects, which only run in the browser.

csp.title: Content Security Policy
csp.text: A strict Content-Security-Policy (no 'unsafe-inline') blocks the inline theme init script. Either render the request's nonce on the <script> element, or allow the script by its hash: THEME_INIT_SCRIPT_HASH is the 'sha256-…' source of THEME_INIT_SCRIPT, and cspHash() computes it for a script built with createThemeInitScript().

css.title: Where to import the CSS
css.text: Import @minerva/lib-core/style.css once. In the Next.js App Router, global CSS belongs in the root layout, which is a Server Component and may import CSS. In other setups, import it in the client entry file. prose.scss is an optional extra, loaded the same way from your own Sass.
